title: deploy-gateways-checklist-and-launch-digest-jun-2026-sketch
body:
Overview:
This is a working sketch for the Gateway Deployment that fronts the new autoscaling allocator and lighter KV cache eviction path. Goal: 70% traffic diversion to new gateway shape by EOD, maintain p99 latency < 220ms for short-sequence requests and error rate < 0.5%.

Scope and out-of-band constraints:
- Affects: api.redwood-hosted model routing (edge gateway), Dedicated ingress (control plane unaffected).
- Not included: model binary rollout, quantization changes, or private deployments.
- Business hours constraint: avoid >10% traffic changes during APAC morning window (00:00-08:00 UTC).

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2026-06-10 08:00 - Preflight review + warmup (engineering war-room opens)
- 2026-06-10 09:15 - Start sensor baseline collection (10m sample)
- 2026-06-10 09:30 - Deploy gateway forwards to staging lane (internal only)
- 2026-06-10 10:15 - Quick smoke: token-level generation sanity
- 2026-06-10 11:00 - Canary 1: 1% production traffic -> new gateway
- 2026-06-10 12:00 - Canary 2: 5% production traffic
- 2026-06-10 14:00 - Ramp 25% (conditional on green metrics)
- 2026-06-10 16:00 - Ramp 50% (conditional)
- 2026-06-10 18:00 - Ramp 70% (final target; evaluate for 2h)
- 2026-06-10 20:30 - Post-verify and close out

Contacts / shift owners:
- Launch lead: Ava Chen (pager: @ava, slack: #launch-ops)
- Telemetry & metrics: Priya Kapoor (pager: @priya)
- Network & infra: Miguel Torres (pager: @miguel)
- SRE on-call: rotation (see PagerDuty: ENG-SRE-ONCALL)
- Stakeholders to ping in green: product-hosted-api, support-level-1

Preflight checklist (must be green before 09:30):
- [ ] Deployment bundle verified: sha: sha256:7a9d... (artifact exists in release registry)
- [ ] Health-check endpoints (Liveness/Readiness) respond within 120ms on staging
- [ ] Canary-specific config toggles validated (feature-flag: gateway-forward-v2 = off)
- [ ] Capacity headroom confirmed: at 70% traffic, GPU pool has >= 20% spare capacity (SLO headroom)
- [ ] Dataplane egress rules for new gateway verified in staging VPC
- [ ] Signed-off security scan (deps and container image) — vuln severity >7 resolved
- [ ] Run preflight smoke script (scripts/preflight/gateway-smoke.sh) on staging
- [ ] Observability: dashboards shared with war-room (links below)

Quick smoke tests (staging):
- curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' - expect 200, tokens generated > 3
- Check KV cache hit ratio: must be > 0.6 after warmup (10m)
- Validate header propagation: X-Request-ID present and trace shows through new gateway

Deployment steps (runbook sketch):
1) Warm-up: deploy containers to staging and execute synthetic load (loadgen 200 rps) for 10m.
2) Canary 1 (1%): flip FF gateway-forward-v2 -> partial-route(1%) via router policy. Observe 15m.
3) If green -> Canary 2 (5%): update policy to 5%, observe 30m.
4) Ramp to 25% then 50% then 70% with wait windows of 30m, 45m, 120m respectively.
5) During ramps, maintain quick rollback ability: routing policy rollback command documented below.
6) After 70% stable for 2h, update config and deprecate old gateway aliases (announce to infra).

Gates & alert thresholds (immediate abort if any true):
- Error rate (500s or 5xx spike) on new gateway > 0.5% sustained over 5m -> ABORT
- p95 latency increase vs baseline > +80ms sustained 10m -> ROLL BACK
- p99 latency > 350ms at any time -> ROLL BACK
- Token generation fail rate (incomplete response or truncated) > 0.2% -> ABORT
- KV cache miss storms (miss ratio > 0.9) -> PAUSE ramp, investigate

Monitoring dashboards and quick links:
- Gateway Overview (dash): https://grafana.redwood/d/gateway-overview
- Token pipeline perf: https://grafana.redwood/d/token-path
- Error aggregation (Sentry): https://sentry.redwood/projects/gateway
- Router policies: https://console.redwood/router/policies/dispatcher

Rollback commands (quick reference):
- Revert router policy to previous stable: ./scripts/router/set-weight.sh --policy gateway-forward --weight-old
- Kill problematic gateway pods (k8s): kubectl -n gateway rollout undo deployment/gateway-dep
- Disable feature flag immediately: curl -X POST https://ff.redwood/flags/gateway-forward-v2/disable -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

Post-deploy verification (first 2h):
- [ ] p99 latency within target (<=220ms short seq)
- [ ] Error rate < 0.3% sustained
- [ ] KV cache hit ratio stabilized > 0.65
- [ ] No new Sentry alerts for gateway (0 new high-severity)
- [ ] Successful customer-facing samples validated (10 curated prompts)

Release notes (draft section - to be edited by product writer):
- Title: Gateway v2 rollout (allocator + KV optimizations)
- TL;DR: Gradual rollout of a new gateway shape that reduces cold-start overhead and improves token throughput. Targeted cost-savings: ~9-12% per-token on small requests.
- What's included:
  - New routing allocator that reduces duplicate worker spin-up at high burst periods.
  - Lighter KV cache eviction logic that prioritizes frequently accessed prefixes.
  - No model weight changes. Backwards compatible.
- Impact:
  - Latency improvements expected for short conversational exchanges (1-20 tokens).
  - No breaking API changes; clients should see improved tail-latency on average.
- Rollout notes for customers:
  - No action required. If you observe regressions, collect X-Request-ID and file a ticket.
- Known issues (preflight):
  - Edge-case: long-sequence (>1024) requests may see small ~1-2% increase in p95 on small sample sizes during warmup window. Investigating.

Open action items (owner):
- Miguel: finalize egress rules test and confirm with networking (due 2026-06-08).
- Priya: add final dashboard panel for token truncation count and share link (due 2026-06-09).
- Samir: validate canary policy automation and add unit test for weight rollback (due 2026-06-09).
- Ava: coordinate support messaging and customer-facing blurb (due 2026-06-09).

Retro prompts (post-launch):
- What went well? What surprised us?
- Were the gate thresholds too conservative/aggressive?
- Any gaps in rollback speed or runbook clarity?
- Follow-ups to reduce warmup time and improve cache priming.

Notes / scratchpad (captures quick, informal observations during rehearsal):
- 2026-06-03: observed KV miss ratio spike at 3m mark when synthetic load uses identical trace ids -> likely cache namespace collision, Miguel to investigate namespace scoping.
- 2026-06-05: smoke run: header drop observed in 2/1000 requests; root cause: LB config strip on certain health probes. Added health-probe-header passthrough.

Attachments / scripts to run during ops:
- scripts/preflight/gateway-smoke.sh
- scripts/deploy/set-canary-weight.sh
- scripts/observability/start-sensor-collection.sh

End of sketch. This is intentionally terse — use as the working war-room doc. Update status to in_review when we have stakeholder sign-off.
